A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, On Universality Classes of Equivariant Networks. The complete main texts, equations and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison across pagination and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 presents mathematical results, symbolic examples and proofs, with no original experimental, simulation, user-study or data-analysis results in the main text or appendices.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical. Its added counterexample and network diagrams do not report empirical outcomes, and the appendices contain mathematical background and proofs.

M1.justification: The network definitions, layer spaces and shallow architectures remain unchanged. Remark 19 examines another instance of the existing coset-representation framework without introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. The architectural examples are mathematical illustrations.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines. Added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics or training budgets.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests or error analyses. The new formal counterexample is assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates and statistical tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries or measured findings are added or revised. The CNN/PointNet symbolic calculations in Section 6.1 remain unchanged; the added mathematical result belongs under T1.

T1.justification: Appendix D substantially rewrites the proof of the central Theorem 13, replacing v1's common-stabilizer argument with basis-independence, block-decomposition and normalized Reynolds-averaging reasoning. New Remark 19 supplies a non-normal-subgroup counterexample to necessity of Theorem 18's normality condition. The main theorem statements otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: separation does not determine approximation power, shallow universality classes admit characterization, and suitable normal-subgroup representations provide sufficient universality conditions.

C2.justification: V1 lists necessity of the normal-subgroup condition as an open question in Section 7. V2 explicitly states that the converse fails, adds Remark 19 in Section 6.2 and removes that unresolved limitation. The limitation to shallow networks remains.

D1.justification: Neither version adds implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware information or code/data access. Changes to mathematical proofs and bibliography metadata do not constitute implementation disclosures.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands its comparison with Stone–Weierstrass, symmetrization and canonicalization approaches. Seven references are added, including Frame Averaging, learned canonicalization and graph-isomorphism/approximation work. The central research positioning remains stable; other reference changes largely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The section structure and most prose are retained. Rewriting is concentrated in related work, Theorem 13's proof and the normality discussion, with additional figure pointers, width-notation cleanup, acknowledgments and bibliography edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds four-panel Figure 1 illustrating layer connectivity and shared weights; v1 has no figures or tables. The overall layout remains similar. The addition contains inconsistencies: Example 3 points to panel b for the permutation-equivariant layer shown in panel c, whose four-dimensional label accompanies three input/output nodes.

improvement.justification: Remark 19 resolves v1's stated normality-necessity question, and the expanded related-work discussion provides useful context. However, the replacement proof of Theorem 13 constructs a basis of arbitrary lambda(M) from full equivariant Hom spaces without justifying that step (Appendix D, p. 22), so its central proof improvement is not established. Together with the new figure's labeling/reference errors, these mixed effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
